metadata.title: Symmetry Transition Preserving Chirality in QCD: A Versatile Random Matrix Model

extraction_notes.note: The paper (PRL format) is organised by run-in \paragraph headings that latex_facts.py does not report as sections, so every node carries an empty section field.

Derivations run into the displayed results mid-sentence ('...yielding \begin{equation}'), so the prose proof nodes end at the last whole sentence before the sentence carrying the result; EP8 (superbosonized partition function) has no proof node since its justification is the same sentence that contains EP7, and is linked by uses edges instead.

Numbered equations retyped as claims (equation was the alternative): the text calls eq. (10) 'the result' and eq. (14) 'a new result', and each is the conclusion of a prose derivation, which needs a result as proves target; rigor semi_formal since the derivations omit steps deferred to a companion paper.
Numbered equation retyped as an external theorem because the text introduces it as a cited Bessel-function identity (Abramowitz-Stegun 9.6.1).
The conjecture spans two sentences: the stated conjecture and the following sentence that ties it to this model's chirality-preserving transition.

Physics background in the introduction (dimensional reduction at high temperature, chiral restoration, applications to graphene and condensed matter), the abstract, the figure caption and the bibliography footnote on counting four-component fermions were not extracted as nodes.

nodes.name: Altland-Zirnbauer tenfold classification
nodes.statement:
There are just ten symmetry classes of Hermitian operators (including RMT) as proven by Altland
  and Zirnbauer~\cite{AltZirn}.
conclusions: There are just ten symmetry classes of Hermitian operators (including RMT)
nodes.statement_short: Hermitian operators (and RMT ensembles) fall into exactly ten symmetry classes.

nodes.name: Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) and chiral Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (chGUE)
nodes.statement: The corresponding random matrix model for the former is the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE)~\cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip} while the one for the latter is the chiral Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (chGUE)~\cite{Shuryak:1992pi,Verbaarschot:1993pm}.
nodes.statement_short: GUE is the random matrix model of 3d QCD and chGUE that of 4d QCD.

nodes.name: Chiral two-matrix model $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement_short: Chiral block matrix $\mathcal{D}$ built from $W=H_1+i\mu H_2$ with Hermitian $H_1,H_2$ and $\mu\in[0,1]$.
nodes.label: RMT-model

nodes.name: Gaussian distribution of $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement: P(\mathcal{D})= \frac{1}{2^N \pi^{N^2}}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\text{tr}(H_1^2+H_2^2)\right].
nodes.label: distribution

nodes.name: Partition function with $N_f$ dynamical quarks
nodes.statement: Z_N^{(N_f)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\prod_{f=1}^{N_{\rm f}}\det(m_f \mathbb{1}_{2N} +\mathcal{D})\,.
nodes.statement_short: Partition function: average of the product of mass-shifted determinants of $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.label: eq:0Zdef

nodes.name: GUE-chGUE interpolation in $\mu$
nodes.statement:
For varying $\mu$ the level statistics of $\mathcal{D}$ 
interpolates between GUE \cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip,Mehta_book} at $\mu=0$ and chGUE~\cite{Shuryak:1992pi,Verbaarschot:1993pm,Mehta_book} at $\mu=1$.
conclusions: the level statistics of $\mathcal{D}$ interpolates between GUE \cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip,Mehta_book} at $\mu=0$ and chGUE~\cite{Shuryak:1992pi,Verbaarschot:1993pm,Mehta_book} at $\mu=1$
nodes.statement_short: The model's level statistics are GUE at $\mu=0$ and chGUE at $\mu=1$.

nodes.name: Microscopic ($\varepsilon$-regime) scaling limit
nodes.statement: The random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ replaces the Euclidean Dirac operator in QCD and its matrix dimension $N$ plays the role of the spacetime volume which will be eventually taken to infinity, keeping $Nm_f^2$ and $N\mu^2$ fixed.
nodes.statement_short: $N$ plays the role of spacetime volume; $N\to\infty$ with $Nm_f^2$ and $N\mu^2$ fixed.

nodes.name: chGUE-to-GUE crossover in high-temperature 4d QCD with twisted boundary conditions
nodes.statement: We conjecture a crossover transition of the spectral statistics of the smallest eigenvalues of the Dirac operator from chGUE (4d) to GUE (3d). {  The kind of transition will be similar if not even exactly as in our model since chirality is preserved in this situation.
assumptions: chirality is preserved in this situation
conclusions: We conjecture a crossover transition of the spectral statistics of the smallest eigenvalues of the Dirac operator from chGUE (4d) to GUE (3d).
The kind of transition will be similar if not even exactly as in our model
nodes.statement_short: Smallest Dirac eigenvalues of hot 4d QCD with twisted b.c. cross over from chGUE to GUE, as in this model.

nodes.name: Euclidean Lagrangian of 3d QCD at finite isospin chemical potential
nodes.label: Lag-phys

nodes.name: Two-matrix model for 3d QCD at finite isospin chemical potential
nodes.statement: One can model this system by the two-matrix model \eqref{eq:0Zdef} with $N_{\rm f}=1$, in close analogy to the 4d case \cite{Osborn:2004}. (Note that $j$ in \eqref{Lag-phys} corresponds to $m_f$ in \eqref{eq:0Zdef}.)
nodes.statement_short: The isospin-chemical-potential Lagrangian is modelled by the $N_f=1$ two-matrix model, with source $j$ playing the role of $m_f$.

nodes.name: Singular values of $W$ correspond to eigenvalues of $\mathcal{D}$
nodes.statement: The singular values of $W$ are bijectively related to the eigenvalues of $\mathcal{D}$ and their statistics were not calculated before.
conclusions: The singular values of $W$ are bijectively related to the eigenvalues of $\mathcal{D}$

nodes.name: Level density vanishes at the origin for $\mu\neq0$
nodes.statement: The microscopic level density will always drop to zero at the origin as long as $\mu\neq0$, see Fig.~\ref{fig.microlevel}.
conclusions: The microscopic level density will always drop to zero at the origin

nodes.name: Partially quenched partition function with $k$ bosonic and $N_f+k$ fermionic quarks
nodes.statement: Z_N^{(k,N_{\rm f}+k)} = \int d\mathcal{D} P(\mathcal{D})\frac{\prod_{j=1}^{N_{\rm f}+k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm f}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})}{\prod_{j=1}^{k}\det(\kappa_{{\rm b}, j} \mathbb{1}_{2N}+\mathcal{D})},
nodes.statement_short: Generating function: ratio of fermionic over bosonic determinants averaged over the ensemble.
nodes.label: eq:Zval

nodes.name: Source variables $\kappa$
nodes.statement: The source variables are $\kappa=\text{diag}(\kappa_{\rm b};\kappa_{\rm f})=\text{diag}((L\varepsilon-i\lambda_{\rm b})\mathbb{1}_k;(L\varepsilon-i\lambda_{\rm f})\mathbb{1}_k,m_1,\ldots,m_{N_{\rm f}})$ with $m_j$ the masses of the dynamical quarks, $L=\pm1$ the sign of the regularization $\varepsilon>0$ and $\lambda_{\rm b/f}$ the source variables for generating the level density.
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa$ collects the bosonic/fermionic regularized sources and the quark masses.

nodes.name: Derivation of the supersymmetric representation (Gaussian integrals)
nodes.statement: In the first step we rewrite the ratio of determinants in~\eqref{eq:Zval} by a Gaussian integral over an $N\times(2k|2N_{\rm f}+2k)$ rectangular supermatrix $V$.
nodes.statement_short: Write determinant ratio as a Gaussian superintegral over $V$, then integrate out $H_1,H_2$ (Gaussian).

nodes.name: Supersymmetric representation of the partition function
assumptions: the integral over $H_1$ and $H_2$ is Gaussian
nodes.statement_short: After integrating out $H_1,H_2$, the partition function is a superintegral over $V$ with quartic supertrace terms.
nodes.label: susy:partiton

nodes.name: Superspace tensor-notation convention
nodes.statement: Note that we suppress the tensor notation with identity matrices  meaning $\kappa$ has to be understood in the $(2k|2N_{\rm f}+2k)$ dimensional superspace as $\kappa\otimes\mathbb{1}_2$ and the Pauli matrices $\tau_j$ as $\mathbb{1}_{k|N_{\rm f}+k}\otimes\tau_j$.
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa$ and Pauli matrices $\tau_j$ are implicitly tensored with identities in superspace.

nodes.name: Superbosonization replacement $V^\dagger V\to U'$
nodes.statement: LV^\dagger V\tau_1\rightarrow \sqrt{N} U'=\sqrt{N}\left(\begin{array}{cc} U'_{\rm bb} & \eta^\dagger \\ \eta & U'_{\rm ff} \end{array}\right),

nodes.name: Grassmann block $\eta$
nodes.statement: The $2k\times(2k|2N_{\rm f}+2k)$ off-diagonal block $\eta$ comprises only independent complex Grassmann variables.
differentia: comprises only independent complex Grassmann variables

nodes.name: Superbosonized partition function
nodes.statement_short: Partition function as an integral over the supermatrix $U'$ with Sdet and Gaussian/$\widehat{\mu}^2$ terms.
nodes.label: susy:partiton.b

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-regime rescaled variables $\widehat{\kappa}$, $\widehat{\mu}$
nodes.statement: Here we have already chosen the rescaling from the $\varepsilon$-regime, namely $\widehat{\kappa}=\sqrt{N}\kappa$ and $\widehat{\mu}^2=N\mu^2$ which are fixed in the large-$N$ limit.

nodes.name: Saddle-point derivation of the chiral Lagrangian
nodes.statement:
There is no supersymmetry and the whole supermatrix consists of the fermion-fermion block, only, $U'=U_{\rm ff}$. For $N\to\infty$ we have to solve the saddle point equation
\begin{equation} U'^2=\mathbb{1}_{2N_{\rm f}}.
\end{equation}
This implies that all eigenvalues of $U'$ are $\pm1$. When diagonalizing $U'$ to its eigenvalues $e^{i \phi}=\text{diag}(e^{i \phi_1},\ldots,e^{i \phi_{N_{\rm f}}})$ we would obtain the Vandermonde term $|\Delta_{N_{\rm f}}(e^{i \phi})|^2=\prod_{a<b}|e^{i \phi_b}-e^{i \phi_a}|^2$ as the Jacobian. This term algebraically suppresses all solutions of~\eqref{sad.eq} in $1/N$ which do not have an equal number of $\pm1$. Thus we integrate only over the coset ${\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})/[{\rm U}(N_{\rm f})\times {\rm U}(N_{\rm f})]$ which is the same as for $\mu=0$ (GUE, 3d QCD), see~\cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip}. This coset can be parametrized as $U'=U\tau_3 U^\dagger$ with $U\in{\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})$.
nodes.statement_short: Large-$N$ saddle point: $U'^2=1$, Vandermonde Jacobian selects equal numbers of $\pm1$, so integrate over the coset $U(2N_f)/[U(N_f)\times U(N_f)]$.

nodes.name: Saddle point equation
nodes.label: sad.eq

nodes.name: Chiral Lagrangian / large-$N$ partition function with $N_f$ flavors
nodes.statement:
Z^{(0,N_{\rm f})}=\!\!\!\!\! \int\limits_{\text{U}(2N_{\rm f})} \!\!\!\!\!\!
d\mu(U)\exp\left[\text{tr}\,U\tau_3U^\dagger \widehat{\kappa}\tau_1-\frac{\widehat{\mu}^2}{2}\text{tr}(U\tau_3U^\dagger\tau_3)^2\right]\!.
assumptions: the partition function in the large-$N$ limit
nodes.statement_short: Large-$N$ partition function: unitary-group integral with mass term and a $\widehat{\mu}^2$ symmetry-breaking term.
nodes.label: k-flav-f

nodes.name: The $\widehat{\mu}^2$ term controls the symmetry crossover
nodes.statement: The symmetry crossover is controlled by the second term. It gives nonzero masses to splitt off the Nambu-Goldstone modes, reducing the coset down to $\text{U}(N_{\rm f})$ for large $\widehat{\mu}$.
conclusions: The symmetry crossover is controlled by the second term.
It gives nonzero masses to splitt off the Nambu-Goldstone modes, reducing the coset down to $\text{U}(N_{\rm f})$

nodes.name: Chiral Lagrangian reproduces leading-order $\varepsilon$-expansion of QCD
nodes.statement: We expect that the result \eqref{k-flav-f} reproduces the leading order of the $\varepsilon$-expansion in QCD for the three areas of applications discussed above.
conclusions: the result \eqref{k-flav-f} reproduces the leading order of the $\varepsilon$-expansion in QCD for the three areas of applications discussed above

nodes.name: Pfaffian form of the $N_f$-flavor partition function
nodes.statement: In~\cite{Kanazawa:2018b} we have even carried out the integral over $U$ explicitly, which yielded either an $N_{\rm f}\times N_{\rm f}$ or an $(N_{\rm f}+1)\times(N_{\rm f}+1)$ Pfaffian determinant, depending on whether $N_{\rm f}$ is even or odd, respectively.
assumptions: depending on whether $N_{\rm f}$ is even or odd, respectively
conclusions: either an $N_{\rm f}\times N_{\rm f}$ or an $(N_{\rm f}+1)\times(N_{\rm f}+1)$ Pfaffian determinant
nodes.statement_short: The unitary-group integral evaluates to an $N_f\times N_f$ or $(N_f+1)\times(N_f+1)$ Pfaffian for even/odd $N_f$.

nodes.name: Level density from the partially quenched partition function
nodes.statement: \rho(\lambda)=\frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}{\rm Re}\left.\partial_{\widehat{\kappa}_{\rm f}}Z_N^{(1,1)}\right|_{\widehat{\kappa}_{\rm b}=\widehat{\kappa}_{\rm f}=L\varepsilon-i \lambda}.
nodes.statement_short: Microscopic level density as the real part of a derivative of $Z^{(1,1)}$ w.r.t. the fermionic source.
nodes.label: level-part

nodes.name: Saddle-point derivation of the microscopic level density
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize the diagonal blocks of $U'$, expand around the saddle point to leading order in $1/N$, integrate out angles to get Bessel functions. The key step is the Bessel identity turning $K_\nu$ into $J_\nu$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.

nodes.name: Quenched microscopic level density of the chGUE-GUE crossover
nodes.statement:
\rho(\lambda)=\;&\frac{2}{\pi}\int_{-1}^1 dx\int_{-\infty}^\infty dy\exp\left[-2\widehat{\mu}^2\left(x^2+y^2\right)\right]\biggl[\left(2\widehat{\mu}^4(y^2-x^2+1)(y^2-x^2)-\widehat{\mu}^2\frac{x^2+y^2}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\lambda^2(2+y^2-x^2)-\frac{1}{4}\right)\notag\\
&\times\sqrt{1-x^2} J_1(2|\lambda|\sqrt{1-x^2})J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})+\lambda^2(1-x^2)\sqrt{1+y^2}J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_1(2|\lambda|\sqrt{1+y^2})\notag\\
&+\left(2\widehat{\mu}^2(y^2-x^2+1)+\frac{1}{4}\right)|\lambda|(1-x^2)J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})\notag\\
&+\left(2\widehat{\mu}^2(y^2-x^2+1)+\frac{1}{4}\right)|\lambda|\sqrt{1+y^2}\sqrt{1-x^2}J_1(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_1(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})\biggl]\,.
conclusions:
\rho(\lambda)=\;&\frac{2}{\pi}\int_{-1}^1 dx\int_{-\infty}^\infty dy\exp\left[-2\widehat{\mu}^2\left(x^2+y^2\right)\right]\biggl[\left(2\widehat{\mu}^4(y^2-x^2+1)(y^2-x^2)-\widehat{\mu}^2\frac{x^2+y^2}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\lambda^2(2+y^2-x^2)-\frac{1}{4}\right)\notag\\
&\times\sqrt{1-x^2} J_1(2|\lambda|\sqrt{1-x^2})J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})+\lambda^2(1-x^2)\sqrt{1+y^2}J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_1(2|\lambda|\sqrt{1+y^2})\notag\\
&+\left(2\widehat{\mu}^2(y^2-x^2+1)+\frac{1}{4}\right)|\lambda|(1-x^2)J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_0(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})\notag\\
&+\left(2\widehat{\mu}^2(y^2-x^2+1)+\frac{1}{4}\right)|\lambda|\sqrt{1+y^2}\sqrt{1-x^2}J_1(2\lambda\sqrt{1-x^2})J_1(2\lambda\sqrt{1+y^2})\biggl]\,.
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form double integral of Bessel $J_0,J_1$ products for the quenched microscopic Dirac level density at coupling $\widehat{\mu}$.
nodes.label: level.density

nodes.name: Non-uniform GUE limit at the origin
nodes.statement: Due to the preservation of chirality in our model, the GUE limit ($\widehat{\mu}\to0$) is not uniform about the origin while it is in~\cite{Damgaard:2010cz,Akemann:2011} when the quark mass vanishes.
assumptions: Due to the preservation of chirality in our model
conclusions: the GUE limit ($\widehat{\mu}\to0$) is not uniform about the origin

nodes.name: Linear level repulsion from the origin
nodes.statement: As we have already pointed out, an exact chirality yields for a complex matrix a linear level repulsion from the origin, though the range where this is happening is of order $\mathcal{O}(\widehat{\mu})$ for small $\widehat{\mu}$.
conclusions: a linear level repulsion from the origin, though the range where this is happening is of order $\mathcal{O}(\widehat{\mu})$ for small $\widehat{\mu}$

nodes.name: Oscillation suppression and uniform chGUE limit
nodes.statement: The oscillations are increasingly suppressed when $\widehat{\mu}$ decreases, whereas the limit $\widehat{\mu}\to\infty$ to the chGUE result is uniformly approached.
conclusions: The oscillations are increasingly suppressed when $\widehat{\mu}$ decreases
the limit $\widehat{\mu}\to\infty$ to the chGUE result is uniformly approached

nodes.name: No differences in the bulk and at the soft edges
nodes.statement: However we do not expect any differences for the spectral statistics in the bulk and at the soft edges.
conclusions: we do not expect any differences for the spectral statistics in the bulk and at the soft edges

nodes.name: Pfaffian point process at finite $N$
nodes.statement: In~\cite{Kanazawa:2018a} we have shown that the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process meaning that all $k$-point correlation functions as well as averages over ratios of characteristic polynomials of the random matrix $\mathcal{D}$ are given by Pfaffian determinants which only comprise three functions.
conclusions: the spectral statistics describe a Pfaffian point process
nodes.statement_short: At finite $N$ all $k$-point correlations and characteristic-polynomial ratio averages of $\mathcal{D}$ are Pfaffians of three functions.

nodes.name: Pfaffian structure persists to infinite matrix size
nodes.statement: This simplifies the analysis greatly and it carries over from finite matrix dimension $N$ to infinite matrix size.
conclusions: it carries over from finite matrix dimension $N$ to infinite matrix size

nodes.name: Infrared QCD Dirac eigenvalues follow the Pfaffian point process
nodes.statement: In particular the statistics of the infra-red eigenvalues of the physical Dirac operators in QCD (say 3d staggered Dirac operators or 3d continuum theory with isospin chemical potential) should also follow this Pfaffian point process and all the consequences related to it.
conclusions: the statistics of the infra-red eigenvalues of the physical Dirac operators in QCD (say 3d staggered Dirac operators or 3d continuum theory with isospin chemical potential) should also follow this Pfaffian point process

nodes.name: Reduce to the fermion-fermion block and pose the large-$N$ saddle point equation
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the fermion-fermion block and pose the large-$N$ saddle point equation

nodes.name: Saddle points have eigenvalues $\pm1$
nodes.statement: This implies that all eigenvalues of $U'$ are $\pm1$.
nodes.statement_short: Saddle points have eigenvalues $\pm1$

nodes.name: Vandermonde Jacobian suppresses unbalanced saddle points in $1/N$
nodes.statement: When diagonalizing $U'$ to its eigenvalues $e^{i \phi}=\text{diag}(e^{i \phi_1},\ldots,e^{i \phi_{N_{\rm f}}})$ we would obtain the Vandermonde term $|\Delta_{N_{\rm f}}(e^{i \phi})|^2=\prod_{a<b}|e^{i \phi_b}-e^{i \phi_a}|^2$ as the Jacobian. This term algebraically suppresses all solutions of~\eqref{sad.eq} in $1/N$ which do not have an equal number of $\pm1$.
nodes.statement_short: Vandermonde Jacobian suppresses unbalanced saddle points in $1/N$

nodes.name: Restrict to the coset $U(2N_f)/[U(N_f)\times U(N_f)]$ and parametrize it
nodes.statement: Thus we integrate only over the coset ${\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})/[{\rm U}(N_{\rm f})\times {\rm U}(N_{\rm f})]$ which is the same as for $\mu=0$ (GUE, 3d QCD), see~\cite{Verbaarschot:1994ip}. This coset can be parametrized as $U'=U\tau_3 U^\dagger$ with $U\in{\rm U}(2N_{\rm f})$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to the coset $U(2N_f)/[U(N_f)\times U(N_f)]$ and parametrize it

nodes.name: Parametrize the diagonal blocks of $U'$ by angles
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize the diagonal blocks of $U'$ by angles

nodes.name: Expand the $z_j$ around the saddle points; one expansion is $1/N$-suppressed
nodes.statement: From the saddle point equation and the properties of ${U'}_{\rm bb}$ and ${U'}_{\rm ff}$ we have to expand the variables $z_j$ as follows: $(z_1,z_2)=(\delta z_1/\sqrt{N},\delta z_2/\sqrt{N})$ and $(z_3,z_4)=(\delta z_3/\sqrt{N},$ $\delta z_4/\sqrt{N}), ~(z_3,z_4)=(\pi/2+\delta z_3/\sqrt{N},\pi/2+\delta z_4/\sqrt{N})$. The latter expansion for $z_3,z_4$ yields an algebraically $1/N$-suppressed term.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the $z_j$ around the saddle points; one expansion is $1/N$-suppressed

nodes.name: Leading-order expansion and Grassmann/fluctuation integrals deferred to the companion paper
nodes.statement: The expansion to leading order in $1/N$ and integration over $\eta$ and $\delta z_j$ is quite lengthy and we omit it here. It is done in detail in~\cite{Kanazawa:2018b}.
nodes.statement_short: Leading-order expansion and Grassmann/fluctuation integrals deferred to the companion paper

nodes.name: Integrate the angles to obtain Bessel $I_j$, $K_j$, then apply the level-density relation
nodes.statement: Afterwards we integrate over $\varphi_1$ and $\vartheta_1$ which yields the modified Bessel functions of first order, $I_j$, and of second order, $K_j$, respectively. Then we are able to use the relation~\eqref{level-part}.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the angles to obtain Bessel $I_j$, $K_j$, then apply the level-density relation

nodes.name: Apply the Bessel identity converting $K_\nu$ to $J_\nu$
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Bessel identity converting $K_\nu$ to $J_\nu$
